The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents U/Sec.166 of M.V.
Act seeking compensation for the damages caused to the vehicle No.KA-51-AJ-0326 in the road traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell: It is the case of the petitioner that on 13.10.2023 the driver by name Manjunath.

D.A. was driving the petitioner's aforesaid EICHER Container Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AJ-0326, which was loaded with Flip Kart company materials from Hosur Industrial area towards Mysore, via Ramanagara on Bangalore-Mysore N.H-275 Bypass Road slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations, while so proceeding at about 4.15 P.M., reached Near Kempegowdanadoddi, Ramanagara Taluk, Ramanagara, wherein the driver of EICHER Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-53-B-6546, which was moving on the left side ahead of the aforesaid Petitioner's EICHER lorry suddenly steered to right side midline of the said road without giving any signal nor switching on the side indicator, nor observing the right side mirror in a rash and negligently, in this process accident occurred, consequent to which the petitioner's aforesaid EICHER Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AJ- 0326 badly damaged as per the IMV Report and the Tax Invoices issued by M/s High Tech Motors and Sri Lakshmi Motors Service Pvt. Ltd.
3.

entities.text: Sri Lakshmi Motors Service Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It is specifically urged that due to the terrific impact the petitioner's vehicle was extensive damaged and after the accident the petitioner's vehicle was towed to service station by hiring the vehicle from accident spot and got repaired and thereby the petitioner has spent Rs.9 lakhs towards replacing new spare parts, tinkering, paining, lathe work, labour charges and Rs.40,000/- towards towing charges.
Further the petitioner's vehicle was in the garage for more than two months, during this period the petitioner has lost the earnings at the rate of 60,000/- p.m i.e., Rs.1,20,000/-.
It is urged that due to the said incident he has been suffered unwarranted mental agony and aggravation.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-53-B-6546.

The respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-53-B-6546 and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.

This respondent has denied that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher Lorry per contra he stated that the accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of petitioner's vehicle.

The respondent No.1 admitted that he is the RC owner of the vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-53-B-6546 and was duly insured Hsl Transport vs Manjunatha G on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27840581/
2 with the 2nd respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
It is further submitted that the driver of the lorry also possess valid and effective driving licence.
It is further urged that in case if court comes to conclusion that the petitioner is entitle for any compensation same is to be fastened on the 2nd Respondent - insurance company.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2 and respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel by filing the written statement to the main petition contending that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and liable to be dismissed.
The respondent No.2 admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Eicher Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-53-B-6546.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the driver of petitioner's vehicle who was driving the vehicle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road and he was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.

Further this respondent contended that the owner and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provision of Sections 134(c)
and 158(6) of M.V.Act.

Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL and further the said insured vehicle did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent act of driver of offending Eicher Canter bearing Reg.No.KA-53- B-6546 and as result the unoffending Eicher Container lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AJ-0326 sustained damages ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum ?
From whom ?
3.
What order and award?
7. The Partner of the petitioner company examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's .
P1 to 23 and Ex.P.28 to 30 were marked on his behalf.
The petitioner also examined the Senior Accountant in Sri Lakshmi Motors Service Pvt. Ltd as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P.24 to 27 documents.

entities.text: Sri Lakshmi Motors Service Pvt. Ltd
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 examined the driver of the offending vehicle as RW.1.

3
Further the respondent No.2 also examined its official as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R.1 to 3 documents.
8. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondents on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1:
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.14,00,000/- together.
In order to prove the factum of negligence the petitioner has mainly relied on Ex.P.2 to Ex.P.9 being police documents.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by driver of petitioner's vehicle, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of Eicher Canter Vehicle bearing No.KA-53-B-6546 for the offences punishable under section's 279 of IPC and u/s 177 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, they have not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
During the arguments the respondent No.2 argued that contributory negligence can be taken into consideration.
On perusal of the written statement in this regard no pleading, hence it cannot be considered.
Further there is no evidence at all to show that there was negligence of driver of petitioner's vehicle.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Eicher Canter Vehicle bearing No.KA-53-B- 6546.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
10. ISSUE NO.2 :
The petitioner in order to prove its case examined its Partner as PW.1, The PW.1 filed evidence affidavit in lieu of examination in chief wherein he reiterated the petition averments.

It is the case of the petitioner that the RC of Eicher Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AJ-0326 is stands in the name of HSL Transport and he being the partner of the transport, the said lorry was met with in the RTA.

That after the accident he has got repaired the Eicher Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AJ-0326 in Sri Lakshmi Motors Service Pvt Ltd., and further he has been purchased cabin assembly to the Eicher Lorry from M/s Hi Tech Motors and Transporter Auto Engineering at Bengaluru and same was rebuilt and got repaired at Sri. Laksmi Motors Service Ltd, Ramangara.

entities.label: ORG

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has spent more than Rs.9.00 lakhs towards replacing new spare parts, tinkering, painting, Lathe work, Labour charges etc and also paid the towing charges of Rs.40,000/- and the said lorry was parked in the garage more than two months, during that period he has lost his earning of Rs.1,20,000/- at the rate of Rs.60,000/- p.m., though the lorry got repaired, its resale value went down.
11. In order to substantiate the same the petitioner has produced Repair Estimation, 3-Tax invoices and towing crane charges bills at Ex.P.12 to 17 respectively.

The petitioner contended that in the Hsl Transport vs Manjunatha G on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27840581/
4 accident the Eicher Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AJ-0326 exhaustively damaged and in this regard he has produced Ex.P4 IMV report.

On perusal of the same it reflects the Eicher Lorry had following damages :
1) Front shape damaged 2) Wind screen glass and wiper damaged 3) Front bumper damaged 4) Cabin full damaged 5) cabin top body damaged 6) Cabin both side door and glass damaged 7) Dash board damaged 8) Front suspension damaged 9) Steering system damaged 10) Head light and indicators damaged 11) Front left side goods body damaged.

12. Further the records discloses that the Eicher Container Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-51-AJ-0326 was left for repair at Sri Lakshmi Motors Service Pvt Ltd., Ramanagara, it has issued service / repair estimate and same is marked at Ex.P.12 for Rs.8,33,256.57.

entities.text: Sri Lakshmi Motors Service Pvt Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further the petitioner has produced Ex.P.13 being the Tax invoice issued by Hi-Tech Motors for Rs.5,79,995/-.
Ex.P.15 being the another tax invoice issued by Transporter Auto Engineering for Rs.80,000/-.
Ex.P.16 is the Tax invoice issued by Sri Lakshmi Motors for Rs.52,926/- and the towing bill for Rs.15,000/-.
In all he claimed Rs.7,27,9121/- towards of repair of vehicle.
13. The advocate for respondent No.2 argued that the depreciation of yearly 10% can be deducted and as per IDV value can be awarded after deduction of depreciation.
The petitioner has repaired excess of the damages in the Road Traffic accident, that can be deducted.

14. On the other hand, the petitioner counsel vociferously argued that the petitioner has produced the MVA report, charge sheet, and as bills for her car repair and contended that due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, the accident took place and his vehicle was damaged in the said accident and he has spent amount for his vehicle repair.
Further contended he has produced bills for repair of vehicle as per Ex.P.13 to 17.

Hsl Transport vs Manjunatha G on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27840581/
5 15.
In this case the petitioner has examined the Accountant of Lakshmi Motors as PW.2.
PW.2 in his chief- examination stated that container lorry bearing No.KA-51-AJ- 0236 was had come to their service centre in the month of Oct- 2023 and Job card issued on 14.10.2023.
Same was repaired and after the payment it was delivered to the petitioner.
He has produced Ex.P.25 to 27.
In the cross-examination he admitted that Ex.P.12 is the quotation, not invoice.
The respondents have not denied the Ex.P.26 and Ex.P.27.
Ex.P.26 is the Job card and Ex.P.27 is the Tax invoice.
Ex . P.27
tallied with the Ex.P.16
and 16 are one and the same.
In the Ex.P.27 parking charges has charged excess, hence it should be deducted.
Except the said parking charges, the repair of the vehicle tallied with damages caused in the Road Traffic Accident as per IMV Report.

It is also tallied with Job card as per Ex.P.26.
16.
It is pertinent here to note that in this case the petitioner has proved that the vehicle is belongs to HSL Transport as per Ex.P.30.
The petitioner is the partner of the HSL Transport.
As per Registration Certificate of HSL Transport the petitioner and his wife are the partners.
It clears that petitioner is the owner of the vehicle being the partner of HSL Transport.
In the cross examination PW.1 stated that his insurer surveyed and stated that Rs.9,50,000/- was loss and they would have pay only 60 to 70%.
Therefore he has not claimed.
But in this regard he has not produced any documents.
Respondents also have not contended that petitioner already claimed through his insurer.
As per the Ex.P.13, 15 and 16 it clears that the petitioner repaired his vehicle as per damages in RTA.
But in Ex.P.16 shows Rs.28,035 as excess.
It is shown as parking charges.
Hence, it should be deducted.

In total the petitioner is entitled Rs.5,79,995/- + Rs.80,000/- and Rs.24,892/- (52,927 - 28,035) = Rs.6,84,887/-.
17.
The petitioner also proved that his vehicle was damaged due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Eicher container lorry bearing No.KA-53-B-6546.

Therefore, when there is an accident and damage to the petitioner's vehicle, there must be a repair of the damaged part of the vehicle and he also proved he repaired the vehicle as per Ex.P.13, 15, Ex.P.16 and Ex.P.26(Job card).
18. In this case, the damage to the petitioner vehicle is proved by documentary evidence.

Therefore,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that, in view of damage caused to the petitioner vehicle, the respondents are liable to pay compensation for such repair.
Therefore, the compensation is to be awarded as Compensation in favour of petitioner.

By considering the damages to the petitioners container lorry, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled a sum of Rs.6,84,887/-
which is rounded off to Rs.6,84,900/- as damages.
19.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
20. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the owner and the insurer thereof are jointly &
severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one Hsl Transport vs Manjunatha G on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/27840581/
6 month from the date of this order.
Hence this tribunal answers issues No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,84,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of incident till its realization.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount the office is directed to release the entire share with interest of the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
